name: Llagar Renovation
notes: Sheet 0 (Baldo Arquitectura, Quintes between Villaviciosa and Gijón, Asturias; a former llagar - cider house - renovated): a traditional Asturian house as a natural extension of the land: walls of local honey-grey stone on the ground floor, big timber sliding shutters across the doorways, a long timber-clad storey tucked under a clay-tile pitched roof with deep timber eaves and a gable end of stone with a timber pediment; at the east an L-shaped wing whose gable end faces the lawn, a timber terrace in the angle; a white traditional house with balconies at its back; open lawn. Inside: a ceiling of cedar-lined boards, a floating fireplace, cement tile floors (last photograph; not modelled). Modelled: the main stone block with its timber upper floor and tile gable roof, shutters and windows, the wing, the neighbour, paving, bollard lights. Guessed: dimensions (21 x 10 m main block), the slope of the lawn, the neighbour's plan. A private home placed at its town only (Villaviciosa).
